title: The Three Fish
text:
In a pond lived three large fish. One was called Forethought, one Ready Wit, and one Whatever Will Be.

One evening some fishermen walked past the pond and stopped to look at it. It was full of fish, they said, and the water was low. Tomorrow they would come back with their nets and catch the lot.

Forethought heard them and called the others together. They should leave tonight, he said, through the stream that led to another lake, while they still could. Ready Wit said there was no need to flee yet; if trouble came, he would think of something. Whatever Will Be said he would not leave the pond where he was born because of some passing talk. What was fated would happen anyway.

So Forethought left that night with his family. The next morning the fishermen came and dragged their nets through the pond. Ready Wit was caught, but he lay perfectly still and pretended to be dead. The fishermen tossed him aside onto the bank, and when no one was watching, he flipped back into the water and escaped. Whatever Will Be thrashed about in the net until the fishermen killed him.
lesson: The best plan is to act before trouble arrives; the next best is to keep your head when it does. Leaving everything to fate is not a strategy.
